# Rise and Battle the Day

## Scripture
"Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be frightened, and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go." – Joshua 1:9

## Reflection
Every morning you wake up, a battle is already waiting. Not against flesh and blood, but against the pull of comfort, the whisper of passivity, and the enemy who wants you to stay soft and sidelined. Joshua faced the same tension. He was stepping into leadership after Moses, staring down fortified cities and armed nations—and God's first word to him wasn't a strategy or a weapon. It was a command: be strong and courageous.

Notice that courage here isn't a feeling. It's an order. God didn't tell Joshua to wait until he felt brave; He told him to act brave because God Himself would go with him. That's the same call on your life, brother. Strength isn't the absence of fear—it's obedience in the presence of it. Your courage is rooted in the character of God, not the size of your obstacles.

So get up. Show up. Take the next hill, whether that's a hard conversation, a discipline you've been avoiding, or a temptation you've been flirting with. The Lord your God goes with you. Now go.

## Daily Challenge
Do 25 pushups, and with each rep say, "Be strong and courageous." Then take on the one hard thing you've been putting off today.
